premise: A talented young batter from a neighborhood club earns a place at a state cricket academy and must rebuild her game after a serious injury.

arc.premise: A talented young batter from a neighborhood club earns a place at a state cricket academy and must rebuild her game after a serious injury.
arc.logline: When a talented young batter from a neighborhood club earns a place at a state cricket academy and must rebuild her game after a serious injury, Mira learns that a lasting cricket career is built between the highlights.

characters.name: Mira Sen
characters.arc: from gifted junior batter to patient team leader

characters.name: The Selection Committee
characters.arc: from distant judgement to earned trust

phases.name: The First Net
phases.turn: Mira earns a trial spot after a patient innings on a cracked community pitch.

phases.name: Away Grounds
phases.turn: Mira learns that different pitches and opponents demand more than natural talent.

phases.name: The Long Recovery
phases.turn: An injury forces Mira to rebuild her technique, confidence, and place in the team.

phases.name: Selection Week
phases.turn: Mira and Kabir face pressure, politics, and one final chance to earn selection.

phases.name: The Deciding Innings
phases.turn: Mira chooses what kind of player and captain she wants to become.

episodes.title: The First Innings 1
episodes.text:
The First Innings 1. Mira Sen had learned that a good innings was built from small choices: leave the ball, trust the footwork, and keep watching the field. The session demanded more than a clean stroke. At her first trial, the coach watched whether she could leave a tempting ball outside off stump. On the last ball of the net, she held her shape and sent a clean drive through the covers. Kabir Rao, waiting to bat, nodded once. The premise sounded simple: A talented young batter from a neighborhood club earns a place at a state cricket academy and must rebuild her game after a serious injury. Mira knew the difficult part was staying ready when nobody was watching.

They trained on a ground where the outfield dipped near square leg and the practice nets had been repaired with mismatched rope. Mira marked her guard, checked the wind, and faced a faster bowler than the one listed on the schedule. Kabir called out advice from the next net, but she learned to hear only what helped. A mistimed shot struck the mesh. She reset, breathed, and played the next ball late.

The afternoon session became a test of patience. Mira wanted to prove she belonged in the academy squad. Kabir wanted to know whether she could score without taking risks that left the lower order exposed. They argued beside the kit bags while rain gathered over the far boundary. Their coach reminded them that a team could not build a season around one player's highlights. They chose the next session carefully, knowing every small habit would show under pressure.

By evening, the trial match had tightened into a contest of singles. Mira stopped chasing the spectacular shot and began placing the ball into spaces the fielders had forgotten. Kabir settled at the other end, turning quick ones into twos and calling early enough to keep them safe. Their partnership was not pretty, but it changed the total and made the opposition captain move 2 fielders.

The innings changed the question. Mira was no longer asking whether she had enough talent to be selected. She was asking what the team would need from her when the pitch was slow, the score was behind, and her timing disappeared. She kept the worn ball from the final over in her kit bag. Kabir did not celebrate. He simply asked whether she would be at training tomorrow, and she gave him an answer that depended on the next morning's work.

At the end of the day, Mira closed the book, tightened the tape around her wrist, and walked back toward the nets before the lights went out. The final entry read: the scorebook records a decision that could change the season.
